name: Inverted Row
summary: A bodyweight horizontal row under a fixed bar that trains the upper back and arms; difficulty is adjusted by body angle and foot position.
setup: Set a bar at about waist to chest height, for example in a squat rack or Smith machine.
Lie underneath and grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Extend the body in a straight line from head to heels, heels on the floor, arms straight.
execution: Squeeze the glutes and abs to keep the body rigid.
Pull the chest toward the bar by driving the elbows back.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower under control until the arms are straight.
mistakes: Sagging hips: squeeze the glutes and abs, or raise the bar to make it easier.
Reaching with the chin or neck: keep the head neutral and pull the chest up.
Short reps: finish with the chest touching the bar and arms fully extended at the bottom.
Too hard to complete reps: raise the bar or bend the knees.
